legend: As part of your contribution in the Great Bubble War, you have been tasked with finding the newly built enemy fortress. The world you live in is a giant 109×109$$$10^9 \times 10^9$$$ grid, with squares having both coordinates between 1$$$1$$$ and 109$$$10^9$$$.

You know that the enemy base has the shape of a rectangle, with the sides parallel to the sides of the grid. The people of your world are extremely scared of being at the edge of the world, so you know that the base doesn't contain any of the squares on the edges of the grid (the x$$$x$$$ or y$$$y$$$ coordinate being 1$$$1$$$ or 109$$$10^9$$$).

To help you locate the base, you have been given a device that you can place in any square of the grid, and it will tell you the manhattan distance to the closest square of the base. The manhattan distance from square (a,b)$$$(a, b)$$$ to square (p,q)$$$(p, q)$$$ is calculated as |a−p|+|b−q|$$$|a−p|+|b−q|$$$. If you try to place the device inside the enemy base, you will be captured by the enemy. Because of this, you need to make sure to never place the device inside the enemy base.
Unfortunately, the device is powered by a battery and you can't recharge it. This means that you can use the device at most 40$$$40$$$ times.
input: The input contains the answers to your queries.

Your code is allowed to place the device on any square in the grid by writing "? i$$$i$$$ j$$$j$$$" (1≤i,j≤109)$$$(1 \leq i,j \leq 10^9)$$$. In return, it will recieve the manhattan distance to the closest square of the enemy base from square (i,j)$$$(i,j)$$$ or −1$$$-1$$$ if the square you placed the device on is inside the enemy base or outside the grid.

If you recieve −1$$$-1$$$ instead of a positive number, exit immidiately and you will see the wrong answer verdict. Otherwise, you can get an arbitrary verdict because your solution will continue to read from a closed stream.
Your solution should use no more than 40$$$40$$$ queries.

Once you are sure where the enemy base is located, you should print "! x$$$x$$$ y$$$y$$$ p$$$p$$$ q$$$q$$$" (1≤x≤p≤109,1≤y≤q≤109)$$$(1 \leq x \leq p\leq 10^9, 1 \leq y \leq q\leq 10^9)$$$, where (x,y)$$$(x, y)$$$ is the square inside the enemy base with the smallest x$$$x$$$ and y$$$y$$$ coordinates, and (p,q)$$$(p, q)$$$ is the square inside the enemy base with the largest x$$$x$$$ and y$$$y$$$ coordinates. Note that answering doesn't count as one of the 40 queries.
After printing a query or printing the answer, do not forget to output end of line and flush the output. Otherwise, you will get idleness limit exceeded. To do this, use:
See the documentation for other languages.

legend.ai: 作为你参与伟大泡泡战争的一部分，你的任务是找到新建的敌方堡垒。你生活的世界是一个巨大的 109×109$$$10^9 \times 10^9$$$ 网格，每个格子的两个坐标都在 1$$$1$$$ 到 109$$$10^9$$$ 之间。
你知道敌方基地呈矩形，且其边与网格的边平行。你们世界的人们极其害怕身处世界边缘，因此你知道基地不包含网格边缘上的任何格子(即 x$$$x$$$ 或 y$$$y$$$ 坐标为 1$$$1$$$ 或 109$$$10^9$$$ 的格子)。
为了帮助你定位基地，你得到了一台设备，可以将它放在网格上的任意格子中，它会告诉你该格子到基地中最近格子的曼哈顿距离。从格子 (a,b)$$$(a, b)$$$ 到格子 (p,q)$$$(p, q)$$$ 的曼哈顿距离计算公式为 |a−p|+|b−q|$$$|a−p|+|b−q|$$$。如果你试图将设备放在敌方基地内部，就会被敌人俘获。因此，你必须确保绝不将设备放在敌方基地内部。
遗憾的是，这台设备由电池供电，且无法充电。这意味着你最多只能使用设备 40$$$40$$$ 次。

input.ai: 输入中包含对你各次查询的回答。
你的代码可以通过输出“? i$$$i$$$ j$$$j$$$”(1≤i,j≤109)$$$(1 \leq i,j \leq 10^9)$$$，将设备放置在网格中的任意方格上。作为回应，你将获得方格 (i,j)$$$(i,j)$$$ 到敌方基地最近方格的曼哈顿距离；如果放置设备的方格位于敌方基地内部或网格外，则返回 −1$$$-1$$$。
如果你收到的是 −1$$$-1$$$ 而不是正数，请立即退出，此时你将看到错误答案的评测结果。否则，你可能会得到任意评测结果，因为你的程序会继续从已关闭的输入流中读取数据。
你的程序使用的查询次数不得超过 40$$$40$$$ 次。

一旦确定了敌方基地的位置，你应当输出“! x$$$x$$$ y$$$y$$$ p$$$p$$$ q$$$q$$$”(1≤x≤p≤109,1≤y≤q≤109)$$$(1 \leq x \leq p\leq 10^9, 1 \leq y \leq q\leq 10^9)$$$，其中 (x,y)$$$(x, y)$$$ 是敌方基地内部 x$$$x$$$ 坐标和 y$$$y$$$ 坐标均最小的方格，而 (p,q)$$$(p, q)$$$ 是敌方基地内部 x$$$x$$$ 坐标和 y$$$y$$$ 坐标均最大的方格。注意，输出答案不计入 40 次查询。
输出查询或答案后，不要忘记输出行末并刷新输出流。否则，你将得到超出空闲限制的评测结果。为此，请使用：
C++ 中的 fflush(stdout) 或 cout.flush()。
其他语言请参阅相关文档。
